result.title: TxnQA: Benchmarking Analytical Reasoning and Evidence Grounding over Transaction Event Sequences
result.summary: Analyzing merchant transaction histories requires dynamic temporal filtering, entity resolution, and aggregation over irregular event streams--operations poorly captured by static tabular or time-series forecasting benchmarks. We introduce TxnQA, an analytical QA benchmark comprising 27 task families (81 templates) alongside a 5-scenario fraud-risk reasoning suite that evaluates both verdicts and supporting evidence over synthetic, privacy-mitigated transaction data. Ground-truth answers are computed programmatically, and model performance is decomposed into format-following rate (FFR), conditional content accuracy (CA), and end-to-end correctness (E2E). Evaluating prompted proprietary baselines and six LoRA-adapted open-weight models shows that adaptation reliably enforces output schemas but leaves arithmetic bottlenecks: Gemma-4-31B-IT and Qwen3-8B attain E2E scores of 0.867 and 0.816, whereas evaluated MoE checkpoints reach only 0.632-0.713. Furthermore, on the 500-instance fraud suite, verdict accuracy frequently exceeds 80%, yet joint accuracy (requiring exact evidence attribution) collapses to at most ~23%. These findings identify schema compliance, semantic calculation, and evidence attribution as three distinct bottlenecks in transaction-sequence QA.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 TxnQA 基准，在合成的商户交易事件流上构建 27 类任务与欺诈风险推理套件，同时评测结论与支撑证据，并把表现拆分为格式遵循率、条件内容准确率和端到端正确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 结论准确率与证据归因联合准确率之间的巨大落差，可能为检验 latent 状态中的视觉证据是否真正支撑答案提供评价思路；但任务为纯文本交易流、无视觉输入与 latent 推理状态，可供核查迁移价值有限。
